title: Let documents.mjs revision --check name a check the change's coverage adds
description:
Found 2026-09-27 recording readable-views-2's receipts: `node .shady2k/documents.mjs revision --check views-check` fails with 'the policy has no check views-check' although a change's Coverage may name checks the policy does not list (views-check, readability), whose receipts stand on the whole revision. The refusal hint of runCheck already prints the whole revision for them. Worked around by recording those receipts against `documents.mjs revision`.

## Done when
revision --check <id> prints the whole revision for an id the policy does not pin (or refuses only an id no policy entry and no coverage could name, saying so), a test covers it, and the integration's receipt instructions say which command to use.

title: Skip the product checks in CI for changes that cannot touch the product, and run once per pull request
description:
Found in the setup 0.33.0 run (madarch-np7): CI runs bun install, check, test and views:check (about 7 minutes) on every push, documents- and tracker-only pushes included, and twice on a branch with an open pull request (push and pull_request).

## Done when
A push or pull request that changes only docs/, .beads/, .shady2k/, .githooks/ or root *.md files runs no product check; pushes run the checks on main only and pull requests once each; the integration's CI line says so.
close_reason: Fixed in e967601: CI on pushes to main and pull requests, skipping non-product paths.

title: A page's links, cross-references and footer navigate, and the reader can always go back, not only through the sidebar
description:
What a person does: opens a document page and clicks a link in its text, a backlink, a footer entry, or wants to return. What happens: per the owner nothing responds to a click inside the page; only the left sidebar moves you. What should happen: every link to another document opens it, backlinks and footer entries navigate, the browser's back returns, and a breadcrumb or the overview link is one click away. Owner: 'Перешел куда-нибудь внутрь, потом вернуться невозможно, потому что ни футеры, никакие клики не работают … только в левой панельке можно перейти.'
## DONE WHEN
On the demo product, a body link, a backlink and each footer entry open their target; browser back and forward follow; a test drives each in the built app.
## Left out
New kinds of links.

The owner, 2026-10-13, on the served demo wiki (Fieldnote): "Получается, что это неюзабельно сейчас."
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Clicking the sidebar logo marked `madarch вики` opens the Product overview.
- [ ] Each visible top-bar breadcrumb segment is independently clickable and opens its represented level: `Продукт` opens the Product overview; `Fieldnote` opens its product group. These breadcrumb links provide the visible in-app way back; the Product overview stays one click away.
- [ ] The generic group page is `/g/<encoded-group>`, keyed by the existing `PageMeta.kind ?? groupOf(path)` identity. It uses the existing localized/fallback group label as its heading and lists only that group’s live pages as links. The group breadcrumb segment and sidebar group heading link to it; the logo and first breadcrumb segment open the overview. No product-specific data is hard-coded.
notes: Owner Addendum 3 (2026-10-13) resolves the earlier group-route blocker: implement the generic `/g/<encoded-group>` page using the existing group identity/label and live pages only; wire both group breadcrumb and sidebar group heading to it, while logo and first breadcrumb go to overview.

title: Isolate every test run in its own scratch home and temporary folder, so no suite leaves anything in the owner's home or the system temporary folder
description:
Found 2026-09-30 during the wiki run: about 87 000 folders named madarch-* had piled up in the system temporary folder (63 490 of them madarch-model-check-*), left by test suites outside the wiki (test/model-check-repo.ts fixtures and others); together with other projects' caches the disk reached 99-100% twice in one night. The wiki's own suites were fixed in madarch-7br.3.2; the rest were not in that task's scope.

Widened 2026-10-09 (owner): during madarch-rtr.2.3 a test ran `madarch new` without a scratch home and left 377 draft folders in the owner's real ~/madarch/products. Cleanliness that depends on each test remembering to redirect its paths fails again; the run as a whole must be isolated.

## Approach (owner's choice, 2026-10-09)
A test preload declared in bunfig.toml (`[test] preload`) creates one fresh scratch folder per `bun test` run and points HOME, MADARCH_HOME and TMPDIR (and any other home-derived path madarch reads, such as MADARCH_WIKI_CACHE) into it before any test file loads, and removes it when the run ends. Spawned commands inherit it. A container was considered and set aside: tests spawn git, bun and Chromium, which a container would have to carry, and CI would differ from local runs.

## Done when
after bun test (full suite, performance tests included) nothing new exists in the owner's home (~/madarch included) or in the system temporary folder, apart from the wiki's content-keyed caches if they are kept on purpose (a check before and after); a test that writes to a home or temporary path without redirecting it lands in the run's scratch folder; the scratch folder is gone after the run, pass or fail; a committed test proves the preload is active (HOME and MADARCH_HOME point inside the scratch folder).

title: Allow the document gate to retire malformed check receipts append-only

During acceptance of madarch-cswc, `node .shady2k/documents.mjs check --phase acceptance --change engine-skills-install-contract --candidate worktree --target main` exits 2 because comment 2415 on madarch-cswc starts with a `check:` receipt missing the required `revision`. A corrected review receipt cannot help because the gate parses and rejects the malformed older comment first. This blocks the change's acceptance gate.

title: Make the reference system's views readable
description:
Decided by the owner on 2026-09-25 after looking at the merged views of madarch-mk5. Rendered by GitHub's own Mermaid renderer in a 1150 px column (a wide screen), 5 of the 8 pages show arrow labels under 12 px (the landscape 7.8 px, storefront 8.3 px, fulfilment 9.6 px, platform 11.7 px, ordering 11.9 px) and 7 of 8 have labels overlapping each other or a box. Causes: merged labels of up to 103 characters widen the diagrams; a topic's consumer is drawn as an arrow into the broker, named for what it does, so it reads as sending; the broker gathers every arrow; in an element's own view the general relation is drawn from the frame instead of its refinement from the module that does it; merged labels mix publishing and consuming in id order.

## Done when
On every page of the reference system rendered by GitHub's Mermaid in a 1150 px column, arrow labels
are at least 12 px and no label overlaps another label or a box (measured by rendering every page
and recorded with the numbers); every arrow carries its row number and every relation behind it is
in that row of the table under its diagram; a topic's publishers and subscribers are marked
(action: send | receive), their arrows drawn from the initiator, dashed, and entered by role; in an
element's own view its module's refinement is drawn, not the general relation from its frame;
likec4 validate and the Mermaid parse still pass.
(Rewritten 2026-09-27 by the owner's decisions: arrows from the initiator instead of from the broker
(madarch-48x.1), and numbered arrows instead of word labels after measurement.)

## Left out
Direct producer-to-consumer arrows through a topic (a derived relation, a later decision); views per environment or state; the server.
close_reason: Criterion met on 6c8f709 (the rewritten Done when): all 8 pages 13.1 px or more with no overlaps, numbered arrows with every relation in the table, publishers and subscribers marked and dashed, the module's refinement drawn, likec4 validate and the Mermaid parse pass. Stage madarch-48x.2 accepted; PR #2 merged by the owner.

title: Decide how the model marks a topic's or queue's consumer
description:
A decision the owner holds (asked 2026-09-25). In the format, publishing to and consuming from a topic are written alike (a relation from the service to the broker naming the topic interface); only the relation's name tells them apart, so a renderer cannot draw an event from the broker to its consumer.

Options: (1) an optional relation field consumes: true for a consumer of a topic or queue interface (a small, explicit format addition; relations without it unchanged); (2) no format change: event relations drawn dashed and labelled with the topic, arrow direction unchanged; (3) inferring from the name: fragile, not recommended.

Recommendation: (1).

Affects: the task that draws events from the broker to the consumer. Meanwhile the labels and the refinement tasks proceed.
close_reason: Owner decided 2026-09-27: an optional relation field action: send | receive on relations through a topic:: or queue:: interface (Codex's proposal, after AsyncAPI 3). Arrows stay drawn from the initiator (from -> to, as every other arrow), labelled by role: 'publishes <topic>' or 'subscribes to <topic>', dashed; no reversed arrows (owner, citing C4: the initiator's arrow).

title: Let engineers start a product with their existing repositories: rename, remote, repo add, bootstrap and clone from the madarch command
description:
Owner, 2026-10-11 ~11:30 MSK, directly: "Нам нужно сделать так, чтобы уже завтра инженеры могли создать репозиторий продукта, подключить туда имеющиеся репозитории и начать работу." The owner approved the plan ("Конечно"). This widens the milestone idea-to-wiki by a scope decision recorded in the charter: the exclusions "the team: bootstrap of a cloned product, several people on one product" and "code repositories beyond the first" no longer hold for the pieces below. Nothing planned is displaced; outcomes 2-5 (madarch-fe1, madarch-0uc, madarch-ls3, madarch-mni) keep their order after it. madarch-mni overlaps: only what this needs is taken from it; the naming conversation stays with the skills (leave it there).

The bundled product-repository program (vendor/shady2k-skills/0.94.0) already exports rename, remote, bootstrap, repo add and where. The madarch command (src/product/cli.ts, scripts/madarch.ts) exposes only new, serve and list. This feature exposes the lifecycle as thin wrappers over the program, with the same refusals and exit codes as the existing commands, and gives engineers one guide page.

## Work
- madarch rename <name> [--product <folder>]
- madarch remote <url> [--product <folder>]
- madarch repo add <name> <url> [--branch <b>] [--product <folder>] (enters the repository in the manifest, then clones it into repos/<name> through bootstrap; an already-present checkout is left alone and reported)
- madarch bootstrap [--product <folder>]
- madarch clone <url> [--home <folder>]: git clone of a product repository into the products home, then bootstrap, then print the folder and how to open its wiki; this is how a second engineer joins
- the default product folder is the current folder's product (the program's where), so the commands work when run inside a product
- the products home stays ~/madarch/products, moved by MADARCH_HOME or --home; tests never write into the real home
- the capability spec (docs/system/capabilities/product-repository.md) and a change record as the documents gate requires
- the engineer's guide: docs/guides/start-a-product.md, with a pointer from README.md; every command copy-pasteable, what each prints, and running setup-shady2k-skills in the product as the product-repository case

## Left out
The naming conversation of outcome 5 (madarch-mni keeps it; the draft is renamed into an example name at most); several people on one product beyond the first clone; remote transport beyond git; agents through MCP or an API (madarch-yhy); work launched from the wiki.

## DONE WHEN
The acceptance walk, in a scratch home: madarch new; rename to an example name; repo add two real small public repositories; remote to a local bare repository standing in for GitHub; push; then madarch clone of that remote into a second scratch home as the second engineer: both repositories appear under repos/, the wiki serves, and a file saved under docs/ shows on its page. Commands and outputs recorded in the run report. Nothing under ~/madarch/products.

title: Make the five lifecycle commands thin wrappers over the pinned program, with their tests
description:
The madarch command gains the five subcommands as thin wrappers over the bundled pinned program's exports (renameProduct, addRemote, bootstrapProduct, addCodeRepository, whereAmI; vendor/shady2k-skills/0.94.0), with src/product/program.ts extended to name them and product.d.mts extended (the declarations are written in this repository, never in the vendored file) with the shapes as the program's own documentation and self-test give them.

Commands and contracts (parent madarch-525o and its brief):
- madarch rename <name> [--product <folder>]: renames the draft's folder in place, keeps the internal id; refuses a name that cannot be used with exit 2 in the program's words.
- madarch remote <url> [--product <folder>]: sets (or replaces) the git remote the program manages.
- madarch repo add <name> <url> [--branch <b>] [--product <folder>]: enters the repository in the manifest, then clones it into repos/<name> through the program's bootstrap; an already-present checkout is left alone and reported as the program reports it.
- madarch bootstrap [--product <folder>]: clones what the manifest declares.
- madarch clone <url> [--home <folder>]: git clone of a product repository into the products home, then bootstrap, then print the product's folder, its id and how to open its wiki; this is how a second engineer joins.
- The default product folder is the program's where: the current folder's product when no --product is given, so the commands work when run inside a product.
- Exit codes and refusal style match the existing commands: 2 for an argument, a product folder, a manifest or a home that cannot be used; 1 when a step (git) failed; errors name what is wrong, one message per error, on standard error; stdout prints facts one per line.
- The products home stays ~/madarch/products, moved by MADARCH_HOME or --home where the command takes it; tests never write into the real home (the scratch-home helpers).
- help and usage text cover the new subcommands.

TDD: watch a behaviour test fail for the intended reason, then the least code. Tests beside the existing ones (test/product-cli.test.ts and neighbours; the scratch-home helpers), through the CLI's main() as the existing tests do where that reaches the behaviour; git-invoking steps use the project's test git conventions (test/git-env.ts).
Doubled: the module's own decisions (which url/name to hand the program, which streams) are madarch's; the lifecycle calls are the program's only.

Check: bun run check; MADARCH_SKIP_PERF=1 bun test; the new tests iterated alone.
close_reason: done

title: A person working in an existing code checkout starts a madarch product around it and keeps working where they are
description:
Agreed with the owner on 2026-10-13. A person runs an agent (Codex, Claude Code) in their own code repository, e.g. ~/repos/iaam, decides to manage the product with madarch, and ends with a product repository under the products home that holds the docs, the model and the tracker, with their checkout as one of its code repositories, nothing moved unless they choose it.

What the owner decided:
- The product repository is separate (~/madarch/products/<name>); code repositories are entered in workspace.yaml and live under its repos/ (untracked).
- `madarch repo add` run for a checkout that already exists on the machine offers three ways: link to it (the default: a symlink, or a directory junction on Windows, which needs no administrator rights), move it into repos/ (branches, uncommitted work and stash kept), or clone afresh. A machine where neither link can be made says so plainly and offers moving or cloning.
- Nothing of madarch is ever written into the code repository (owner: "В репозитории с кодом не должно быть частей madarch"). A checkout outside a product finds its product by scanning the products home for a repos/ entry that links to it; madarch, the wiki and describe-repository read a linked checkout as a checkout and never clone over it.
- The product repository explains itself to the person: its README says what the product repository is, what docs/, model/ and repos/ hold, and that `make init` builds the whole workspace (clones or links every declared repository, connects the tracker); the Makefile is a thin wrapper over a madarch command that works the same on Windows, where make is usually absent.
- The person is told to restart their agent from the product folder, where the docs, the tracker and the code are all in reach; a command such as `madarch work iaam` may open that place (owner: "Можешь быть даже сделать команду типа madarch work iaam").
- The skill set's side (its setup hints once at madarch in a project with no product repository; its product detection follows the link) is filed in the set's own tracker.

## DONE WHEN
From ~/repos/iaam (a real git checkout with a local branch and uncommitted work), one guided path ends with ~/madarch/products/iaam whose wiki serves the iaam code repository through a link, the checkout still in place with its branch and uncommitted work untouched, no file added to it, `madarch list` naming the product, the agent restarted from the product folder seeing docs and tracker, and `make init` on a fresh clone of the product reproducing the workspace; the same walk on Windows with a junction.

## Left out
The tracker store off the branches (madarch-tjum); multi-machine sync of the link (links are per machine by design); importing the code repository's own history into the product.

This confirms the epic's `madarch repo add` (link default, move, clone; junction on Windows). The owner also asked that the command ask the person how to connect each repository ("нужно спросить у человека как он это хочет сделать"): link to an existing copy (offering a found matching checkout as the default path), clone, or move. A Makefile and scripts/init.mjs were briefly added to shady2k/madarch-product (37280563) and are being removed.

title: The wiki's Starlight engine fails to build when the wiki cache root is the default under the owner's home folder
description:
Found 2026-10-02 standing both engines' wikis of the reference system up for example.

What a person does: builds a wiki with the Starlight engine and no MADARCH_WIKI_CACHE set, so the cache root is the default under the home folder (XDG ~/.cache/madarch/wiki).

What happens: the build exits 1 with the engine's output: astro/vite refuses with "No cached compile metadata found" for @astrojs/starlight/dist/components/Page.astro, and the main-module id it names is mangled — the project root joined onto the cache's absolute path with its leading slash dropped (source/home/dev/.cache/madarch/wiki/template-…/node_modules/…). The same happens under node 24 directly, so it is not the bun runtime.

What should happen: exit 0 with the built site's path (capability wiki, requirement result).

Measured on this machine (same template, same pages, only the named variable changed):
- project under /tmp, node_modules symlinked at the default cache under /home/dev/.cache: build fails;
- project under /tmp, node_modules symlinked at a cache under /tmp (MADARCH_WIKI_CACHE, as the tests move it): build passes, 90 pages;
- the same project, node_modules copied (not symlinked) from the failing /home/dev/.cache install: build passes, 82 pages.

So the trigger is the engine's symlinked node_modules (linkStarlightNodeModules in src/wiki/starlight.ts) resolving into the default cache location, likely a path mishandling in the pinned astro 7.3.5 / rolldown-vite. Untested: whether a project folder also under the home folder fails the same way.

Workaround while deferred: point MADARCH_WIKI_CACHE at a folder outside the home cache (the gated tests already do).

Disproved by: a Starlight build with the default cache root succeeding on a machine with the pinned toolchain, or the trigger shown to be a machine-specific install rather than the symlink-to-default-cache path.

## Done when
- a real Starlight build with the default cache root (no MADARCH_WIKI_CACHE) succeeds on a clean user account, or the writer stops symlinking node_modules from a cache the engine cannot resolve through, naming what replaced it;
- the pinned template's bun.lock stays reproducible: two builds of the same repository still give byte-identical source trees.

title: Keep the query engine's buffer pool from filling under thousands of updates without a rebuild
description:
Found 2026-09-30 by the rework worker of madarch-ti6.2 (change server-views), measured with LadybugDB 0.20.4 under Bun 1.4.2, every query result closed.

## What was measured
- The engine's update path (update -> removeRelation/closeEdge, inserts) grows RSS about 115 KB per update call; with no reads in the loop and a rebuild every 500 calls, the 256 MiB buffer pool is exhausted ('Buffer manager exception: Unable to allocate memory! The buffer pool is full and no memory could be freed') after 5 032 updates and 10 rebuilds. At 2 000 calls RSS climbs linearly from 126 to 356 MB.
- Closing results does not change it (169 157 against 172 506 bytes per call, within noise); reads amplify it through statement churn but do not cause it.
- The read path is bounded: 24 000 dependents and view calls plateau near 160 MB.
- The engine opens new Database(':memory:', 256 MiB, false, false, 4 GiB), so autoCheckpoint stays at its default; the mechanism (WAL, version pages, allocator retention) is not yet known.

## Why it matters, and why not now
The MVP's server updates a graph's engine once per model sent and rebuilds it at start, so thousands of updates between restarts are far off; a server receiving models from CI or webhooks (live-graph) would reach it within days.

## Done when
The cause is found (a checkpoint, a periodic rebuild from the history, or a LadybugDB defect reported with a reproduction), and a test of at least 10 000 updates with rebuilds, yielding between batches, stays under a stated memory bound, skipped with the performance tests.

comments.author: claude-coordinator:shady2k@vm-agents:feature/registry-integrity
comments.text:
Deferred out of live-graph's outcome 1 by the owner, 2026-10-07 ("Я предлагаю этим заняться позже, это нас не блокирует" / "Убери это требование"). Revisit before outcome 3 (madarch-tah) starts: a server fed by CI reaches the bound within days.

Where it stood (run madarch-l19, worker l19-3-mem, 2026-10-02): growth is linear on the update path, ~10.3 MB per 250 updates (137 -> 294 MB over 4000, heading past the 400 MB bound); a disk-backed engine did not help; a smaller buffer pool makes LadybugDB fail. A probe rebuilding the engine from the history every 1000 updates plateaus at 185-192 MB with identical answers: the retained memory is the engine's, not the data's. Proposed mechanism, not yet decided: rebuild the engine from the history when growth exceeds a budget (e.g. +64 MB over its build). Open: the cause inside LadybugDB (not reported upstream); rebuild cost and its peak on a large model (measured only on a one-element model). The measured test and the probe are uncommitted in the worktree ~/.herdr/worktrees/madarch/w-l19-3-memory (test/query-engine-update-memory.test.ts, probe-rebuild-cycle.ts).

title: Let the wiki's agent improve itself through the product's own skills, each change replayed on past cases and accepted by the owner
description:
Idea from the owner, 2026-10-09: the wiki's agent improves itself. Each product repository already holds `skills/`, the team's own skills for that product, which is the natural first place.

Three levels, rising in risk: (1) the product's own skills: the agent sees it is corrected the same way again and again and proposes a change to a skill in `skills/`; (2) the shared skill set, another repository, reached the way a skills issue is filed today; (3) madarch's own code, as a feature run. At every level the change goes through the same path: a tracked task, a pull request, a replay on recorded past cases showing it does better and breaks nothing, and the owner's acceptance. Without that measure it is drift, not evolution.

Related: the owner's lifemodel project changes its own code by commits with an automatic revert; see the idea on lifemodel as the first outside agent.

Would show it is worth it: corrections of one kind stop recurring after the agent's own change to a product skill, measured on the replay.
Left out: changes to another repository without its own review and acceptance.

title: A CI or developer-machine runner uploads facts to the server API when it has no repository access
description:
Owner decision (2026-10-12 ~22:40 MSK, /tmp/madarch-run-iuc/note-storage-boundary.md, decision 0023): code itself never leaves its network. A runner in CI or on a developer machine (feature 0007's ingest surface) uploads imported facts to the server API when the server has no repository access; each fact carries its evidence (source system, ref or commit, record id) and is READ-ONLY in the wiki (authored entities stay writable, provenance 0005).

## DONE WHEN (when opened)
A runner without git access to the product repositories uploads facts through the server API with evidence attached; the server stores them in its fact log with provenance; an uploaded fact renders read-only in the wiki with its evidence named; an upload without evidence is refused naming the missing field; review converged.

title: Take lifemodel as the first outside agent of agent-access: working with the wiki over MCP, and developing the product through its process
description:
Idea from the owner, 2026-10-09: take lifemodel, the owner's own proactive agent project (it acts when pressure builds rather than when polled, changes its own code by commits with an automatic revert, and runs tasks through prime-agent), as an agent working with the product in madarch.

Two roles, kept apart: (1) a conversational agent in the wiki: decision 0017 already lets a person's own agent connect through MCP or the API by the same checked write path, so madarch depends on nothing of lifemodel's and keeps its own server agent for people without one; (2) a developer of the product: lifemodel changes itself without a human step, but madarch's or a product's code only by that repository's process (tracked task, checks, pull request, the owner's acceptance).

Where they meet: the agent-access milestone (MCP and API, madarch-yhy) could take lifemodel as its first outside agent and be accepted on its real work with the wiki, not a synthetic client. Its proactivity fits the wiki: noticing open questions, stale documents and unanswered comments.

Would show it is worth it: when agent-access is chartered, lifemodel has passed its own instance-1 milestone and can hold a session against madarch's MCP.
Left out: making madarch's built-in agent lifemodel.

title: Publish a product release over two sources, joined at the contract boundary
description:
Outcome 2 of live-graph (charter docs/milestones/live-graph.md). product.yaml names the product's member sources and the corpus custody (today the single repository's docs/product/, movable later without changing identity or URLs); a release is published atomically from one manifest pinning every artifact by digest — never synthesized from the latest received state — and publishing validates that every referenced artifact exists and is intact; the landscape joins sources at the contract boundary only; an id clash across sources is reported naming both sources, never merged last-writer-wins; a thin portal builds from a pinned release (shared navigation, product overview, per-source namespaces). title: Work with the wiki through an agent in a chat beside each page: answer questions and comments, create and edit entities
description:
Idea from the owner, 2026-10-09, discussing the wiki. Decision 0017 already chose it ("a chat beside every page"); the idea-to-wiki charter keeps it out of that milestone, and nothing in the tracker carried it until now.

Beside each page, a person writes what they want and an agent works with them on the wiki: answers questions about the product, answers comments, creates documents and other entities, edits the page. It knows the page and the graph around it, writes through the same checked path, each change its own commit so undoing it is one action, and waits for no confirmation. The agent runs on the madarch server with the skill set's behaviour; a person's own agent connects through MCP or the API instead (see the idea on lifemodel as the first outside agent).

Would show it is worth it: in the milestone walk the owner keeps asking an agent outside the wiki to do what the page in front of them should take.
Left out: several people editing one page at the same moment (0018's revisit condition).

title: Lay the review report's problems on the diagrams in our own viewer
description:
Idea from the owner, 2026-09-27, planning madarch-utk. Decision 0001 foresees our own viewer among the frontends; the MVP charter excludes it.

A viewer that shows the views and, on them, the model check's and the review report's findings: a cycle's arrows marked, an element whose document claim is stale greyed, a click on an element or arrow opening its evidence at its commit. The findings already name model ids (madarch-utk), so the report needs no rework for this.

Would show it is worth it: architects reading the review report ask where on the diagram a finding is.
Left out: editing the layout by hand (the vision excludes a canvas).

title: The engine reads nothing of the skill set by name: open questions, the audience, the stages' expected records and the record folders come from the product's manifest
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The per-stage expected records live in the product manifest (docs/kinds.yaml) and are declared once; the skill set computes completeness, not madarch.
- [ ] The contract defines the skill set's completeness result as a file under docs/ with a published schema and pinned conformance cases. The wiki renders that result when present and renders no completeness findings when absent.
- [ ] The engine no longer computes missing completeness in src/wiki/stages.ts; it only renders the supplied result. The skill-set-side writer remains outside madarch-d7v3.2.
- [ ] The completeness result is a committed docs/ file in the product repository and is treated as the truth at that commit’s time; its published schema includes the computed date and source revision, and the wiki displays the localized “as of” date without recomputing.
notes:
Owner decision 2026-10-13, relayed from the skill-set session (comment 2522): completeness is the skill set's calculation. This engine task updates the contract for per-stage expectations in docs/kinds.yaml and for the generated completeness file under docs/ (schema plus conformance cases), renders the file only when present, and removes madarch's src/wiki/stages.ts missing-completeness calculation. The skill-set writer task is external and remains out of scope.
Owner follow-up 2026-10-13 (newest source comment 2524): completeness is a committed product-repository docs/ snapshot at the commit’s time, not a live calculation. The schema must include the date and product revision it was computed for; the wiki presents the localized as-of date and never recomputes.

comments.author: claude-code:shady2k@vm-agents:main#916b13ad
comments.text: The owner's rule restated (2026-10-13): 'Наш движок не должен содержать никаких данных. Если стартуем его с пустой папкой, то на главной показываем краткую инструкцию что делать.' So: no built-in stage list, no default kinds, groups, labels or expectations — everything the wiki shows of a product comes from the product's manifest and documents. The engine's own words are only its functions' UI (buttons, errors, the empty state). Started on an empty folder (no manifest, no documents), the home page shows a short instruction of what to do next (create a product with madarch new, or add a manifest; where the skill set fits). DONE WHEN gains: an empty folder served shows that instruction and nothing else; a test pins it.

comments.author: claude-code:shady2k@vm-agents:main#916b13ad
comments.text: The owner's decision (2026-10-13, given in the skill set's session, relayed by its agent): 'Считать должен ты, madarch - движок, он только отображает.' Completeness is the skill set's to compute, not madarch's: per stage and per kind which expected kinds have no document, which required links are unfilled, which open questions are unanswered. madarch only renders the set's result and decides nothing. For this task: (1) the per-stage expectations become manifest data in docs/kinds.yaml (declared once, the definition of complete the set computes against); (2) the contract gains the completeness result: a file the set writes under docs/ with a published schema and conformance cases like the registry's, and the wiki renders it when present, nothing when absent; (3) the engine's own 'missing' computation in src/wiki/stages.ts leaves (it is that computation). Set side: skills-product-completeness-niv6.

The set-side writer (`skills-product-completeness-niv6`) is outside this task.

title: Make the query-engine long-run memory check independent of what ran before it in the same process
description:
Debt found 2026-10-09 during the madarch-rtr run (stage 1 acceptance), on this machine, while running
the project's full stage checks. It is pre-existing and off that feature's path; nothing in that
change touches the query engine or its tests.

## What was measured
`test/query-engine-long-run.test.ts` asserts the whole run stays under 400 MB
(`expect(Math.max(...curve)).toBeLessThan(400)`). That number is measured on the **process** that runs
it, so it depends on what ran before it in the same `bun test` process:

- the file alone: RSS 159-163 MB, curve flat (slope -0.14 MB/batch), passes;
- the same revision, `bun test test/query-engine-performance.test.ts test/query-engine-long-run.test.ts`
  in one process, perf file first: RSS 436-440 MB, curve flat (slope 0.05, thirds gap 0 MB), **fails**;
- the whole suite (`bun test`, 1234 tests across 55 files): RSS 608-620 MB, curve flat, **fails**.

In every case the shape is the bounded one the test exists to prove (a flat plateau, a small
prepared-statement cache); only the absolute level differs. CI on GitHub runners is green for the same
full suite.

## Why it matters
A required check that is red on the development machine while the file alone is green makes every
stage acceptance ambiguous: the reader cannot tell a real regression from the process's accumulated
allocations, which is exactly the case this test should decide.

## Done when
The check decides the same thing wherever it runs: its bound is measured against a baseline the check
itself establishes (RSS at the start of its own curve, or a bound per batch), or the long-run file is
run in its own process by the check that requires it, and the full suite is green on this machine.

comments.text:
Decision (gap closed alone), coordinator, 2026-10-08: the change makes a current requirement false unless the model history carries the new compiled arrays, so madarch-hnq.1.4 is added to stage 1 to close it.

What I found: src/history/assertions.ts decomposes a compiled model into one assertion per kind of seven (element, interface, relation, category, zone, environment, state) and assembles a model back from exactly those kinds. compiled-model/shape gains entities and scenarios (madarch-hnq.1.1, .1.2), so a compiled model holding them would be stored without them and would not read back as compiled — which is exactly what the current requirement model-history/lossless promises. The change's Coverage does not name model-history, and its Preserved contracts do not either, so this was an oversight in the change, not a decision against it.

Why I did not stop: the alternative closures both need the owner. Filing the limitation as debt and leaving model-history/lossless false would be a weaker acceptance, and correcting that spec sentence would be a new delta in the change record, which changes its approval digest and would need a fresh approval. Carrying the new arrays through the history keeps every present document true and leaves the change's decisions untouched.

What I decided: entities and scenarios are each source's exclusive claim, like elements, interfaces and relations (CLASHABLE_KINDS), not shared vocabulary like zones, categories, environments and states. A second source declaring an existing entity or scenario id is refused, naming the id and the other source; a data entity is a repository's own declaration of its data, and a use case is one repository's, so silently merging two declarations would be worse than refusing.

Where it lands: task madarch-hnq.1.4 under stage 1, after madarch-hnq.1.2, in src/history/** and src/adapters/**, with the change record's Tasks line extended (the Tasks line is not part of the approval digest, so the owner's approval of 2026-10-08 still stands; the feature document check is clean).

title: Give a worktree its own tracker database when connecting it
description:
Found 2026-09-25 starting the readable-views run in a git worktree (.claude/worktrees/readable-views). br discovers the main checkout's .beads/beads.db from a worktree, so sh .shady2k/connect.sh imported the worktree's export into the main checkout's database, and every br write in the worktree then rewrote the main checkout's .beads/issues.jsonl, leaving the main checkout dirty and the worktree's export stale. Worked around in the run by BEADS_DB=<worktree>/.beads/beads.db on every br call.

## Done when
connect.sh, run in a git worktree, creates and uses the worktree's own database (and says how br calls there reach it: an env file, a wrapper, or br's own config), the integration names it, and a test proves that a br write in a connected worktree changes only the worktree's export.

## Left out
Changing br itself.

title: Read the product's pages in the wiki in a comfortable typography and layout: navigation, focus mode and design tokens the editor will share
description:
Added to idea-to-wiki by the owner on 2026-10-09, in conversation, as a scope addition (recorded in the charter's scope decisions). The owner likes the typography of Zettlr, a Markdown editor for the desktop, and wants the wiki to read like it.

Starts after madarch-rtr lands: the wiki app (wiki/app, React 19 + Vite + react-markdown) exists only on that feature's branch, and today it has no stylesheet at all, so every page shows the browser's default HTML.

The work:
- a short research first (to-research): the typography Zettlr ships (fonts, measure, line height, heading scale, vertical rhythm, quotes, code, lists, tables) and the screen-typography guidance it rests on, from primary sources;
- shared design tokens: font families, a type scale, spacing, colours, a light and a dark theme following the system setting; kept in one place so the editor of madarch-j0a reuses them;
- the layout shell (added by the owner the same day, see the comment): a left navigation of the product's documents grouped by kind with the current page highlighted, the document in the centre, a focus mode hiding the panels, the navigation in a menu on a phone, and a closed place for the right context panel;
- the reading styles of the home page and of a document page built on those tokens: a text column of about 60 to 75 characters, line height about 1.5, a heading scale with a steady rhythm, readable quotes, code blocks, lists and tables.

Zettlr is GPL-3.0: its ideas are taken, not its code, stylesheets or fonts under a licence madarch cannot carry.

## Done when
In the browser walk of a fixture product holding headings of every level, paragraphs, a list, a quote, a code block, a table and a long line, each page's text column measures 60 to 75 characters, body line height is 1.4 to 1.6, no element overflows the column at 1150 px and at 390 px width, the dark theme follows the system setting, every page of the fixture is reached from the left navigation in one click with the current one marked (visually and by its accessibility attributes), the focus mode hides both panels and brings them back, and on a phone the navigation opens from a menu without narrowing the text; the numbers are recorded with the walk. A page rendered with the browser's default styles, or a value outside those ranges, disproves it.

## Left out
Search (madarch-o0d); the context panel's content (madarch-fe1, madarch-0uc); the editor, the Markdown and history modes and any editing (madarch-j0a, next milestone); the chat (madarch-cuu); the diagram tabs' own styling; the static Starlight export; a theme switch inside the app.
close_reason: accepted at idea-to-wiki close (the standing follow-ups deferred, returned whole)

title: Find the typography Zettlr ships and the screen-typography guidance behind it, and propose the wiki's design token values
description:
The research madarch-iuc starts with (to-research), before any style is written.

Questions:
- What typography does Zettlr ship for its editor and its preview: font families and their licences, base size, measure, line height, heading scale, paragraph and heading spacing, quotes, code, lists and tables, and its light and dark themes?
- What screen-typography guidance do recognised sources give for long-form reading (measure, line height, scale, rhythm, contrast), and where does Zettlr follow or depart from it?
- Which fonts can madarch ship or reference under its own licence, with a fallback stack for macOS, Linux and Windows?

Primary sources only (Zettlr's own repository and documentation, the guides' own texts), each claim cited. Zettlr is GPL-3.0: the report describes values and choices, it copies no code or stylesheet.

## Done when
A research note kept with madarch-iuc answers each question with citations and proposes the token values (fonts with fallbacks, type scale, spacing, line height, measure, light and dark colours) the feature will implement, each with its source; a question left unanswered is named as open.

title: Choose the wiki app language: Russian and English, react-i18next
description:
The owner asked for a language choice (2026-10-11 ~12:10 MSK, directly): Russian and English, react-i18next. Runs beside the mockup-conformance rework (madarch-iuc.12); the worker may take it after the visual items of note-luna-owner2.md, on the same branch feature/iuc-luna. The full plan is in the note the owner wrote (/tmp/madarch-run-iuc/note-i18n.md) and carries: the library choice with message catalogues en and ru as JSON under wiki/app/src/locales/, every chrome string through it (sidebar, top bar, tab strip, eyebrows, home overview, status bar with Russian plural forms, error/empty states, aria-labels, tooltips), document content NOT translated; a UI language switch remembered in localStorage with the browser-language default; dates and counts through Intl in the chosen language; the mockup's Russian wording as the ru reference; tests for key parity in both catalogues, the switch changing and persisting the chrome, and the ru plurals; ru pairs against the mockup plus one en pair.

- Library: react-i18next with i18next (the common choice for React); message catalogues en and ru as JSON in wiki/app/src/locales/. Every string of the app's chrome goes through it: sidebar, top bar, tab strip, eyebrows (document kinds), home overview, status bar (Live / Reconnecting, words with plural forms: 1 слово, 2 слова, 5 слов), error and empty states, aria-labels and tooltips. Document content is the product's own and is not translated.
- Choice: a language switch in the UI (a small control in the sidebar footer or the top bar, the owner will judge the place in the pairs), remembered in localStorage; the first default follows the browser language (ru* -> Russian, else English).
- Dates and counts through Intl (RelativeTimeFormat, PluralRules) in the chosen language.
- The mockup's Russian wording is the reference for ru: "Обзор продукта", "Документы", "Пространство продукта", "Продукт / ..." and so on.
- Tests: every key present in both catalogues (a test fails on a missing key), the switch changes the chrome and persists, plural forms for ru.
- Pairs: render the ru pairs against the mockup (it is Russian), plus one en pair.

title: Serve and wiki:demo keep serving a stale wiki/app built from earlier sources
description:
The owner pulled main to 58fc5c0a (2026-10-11 10:48 MSK) and ran bun run wiki:demo. The wiki served the OLD app (boxed home cards, no tab strip, the brand "m. Fieldnote"): the app built from the sources before f5e20cc.

Cause (verified this run): src/product-wiki/app.ts builds wiki/app/dist only when dist/index.html is absent, and never rebuilds while the dist is there. The checkout's dist had been built 2026-10-10 from the old sources; after pulling, serve kept serving it.

Fix (this finding's plan):
- serve (and wiki:demo) rebuilds the app when its sources changed since the dist was built: record a hash of wiki/app's sources and lockfile into the dist at build time, compare on start, rebuild with a one-line notice when they differ. No change -> no rebuild.
- Test: build, change a source file, start again -> built again; no source change -> not rebuilt.
- Update the product-wiki capability spec's requirement `app` wording to carry the rebuild-on-change rule.

Temporary measure already applied by the coordinator: the stale dist deleted and rebuilt in the owner's checkout (index-CZ46ApAU.js with /api/events), so the owner saw the fresh app.

title: The registry reader refuses a link field named after a generic document field (id, kind, status, links), as contract v1 requires
description:
Decision 0021's amendment and the contract-v1 proposal require a refusal when a kind's link field is named id, kind, status or links (the generic fields madarch reads itself). src/product/contract.ts (296-319) and src/product/schema.ts (25) accept such a field; no conformance case covers it. Found by the closure review of the standalone-contract-v1 spec sync (madarch-m8eo.1), 2026-10-13; m8eo.1's closure waits on it.

What a person does: declares in docs/kinds.yaml a link field named status. What happens: the registry reads clean. What should happen: refused naming the file, the line, the field path and the words, like the other registry refusals.

## DONE WHEN
parseContractText refuses each of the four names as a link field with file, line, path and words; examples/contract/registry-cases.json carries a case for it; contract:check passes; the skill set is told so its pinned copy of the cases mirrors the new case deliberately.

title: madarch speaks A2A: agents hand madarch work and madarch hands work to agents, as the form of the agent API (0022)
description:
Owner's idea, 2026-10-14: «А что если наш madarch будет слушать протокол A2A и сможет общаться с агентами?»

Agent's position (same day): A2A (Agent2Agent, Linux Foundation; agent card at /.well-known/agent-card.json, JSON-RPC over HTTP, tasks with messages and artifacts, SSE streaming, push notifications) fits decision 0022's published agent API rather than a new direction. Split by what each protocol is for: MCP for an agent that uses madarch as a tool (read the graph, write a document, comment, claim work) — already the planned way in 0017; A2A for madarch handing work to an agent and following it as a task (a comment that needs an answer, a document to write, later a tracker work item), which 0022 now routes to Lifemodel through a bespoke channel plugin; with A2A, Lifemodel and any other A2A agent plug in the same way. madarch stays no executor (0022, and the tracker discussion: it does not launch agents): A2A only messages agents that already run. Caveat: the coding agents in use (Claude Code, Codex, omp) speak MCP natively, not A2A as servers, so A2A pays off with agent platforms (Lifemodel, ADK, LangGraph, cloud agent services).

Review when the agent API (0022) or the tracker milestone (madarch-lk4r) is shaped: decide whether the agent API's outgoing side is A2A.

title: Record madarch's diagnosability conventions: log levels, request and trace ids, error causes
description:
Found in the setup 0.40.0 run (madarch-f9w), by the setup skill's diagnosability item: the repository records no conventions for what a log line carries at each level, how a request or trace id is threaded through the server, or how an error keeps its cause; and nothing says which of them a test or a review may rely on. title: Make madarch's checks and messages independent of the unrelated nocx repository
description:
Found 2026-10-07 while resuming madarch-l19: the run's coordinator spent most of an hour trying to rebuild a checkout of nocx to run the server e2e test. The owner: "Почему это тест требует репозиторий nocx? Наш репозиторий не имеет к nocx никакого отношения."

## What is wrong
madarch's checks and texts depend on nocx, an unrelated repository of the owner:
- test/server-views-e2e.test.ts (added f93b9bc, 2026-10-01, as the server-views acceptance) sends nocx's model from a local nocx checkout named by MADARCH_NOCX and pinned to commit 3f0e46e (source github.com/shady2k/nocx). The model it sends lives on branch madarch-skill-run in the nocx repository. Without that checkout on this machine those tests cannot run; on another machine they never can.
- Product error messages give "github.com/shady2k/nocx" as their example: src/server/http.ts (~302, 459, 588), src/server/sources.ts (~134-140), src/send/send-model.ts (doc comment ~126).
- Current specs and records name it: docs/system/capabilities/server.md scenarios, docs/glossary.md:108, docs/decisions/0013; tests test/send-model.test.ts, test/server-sources.test.ts, test/server-http.test.ts.
Origin: the MVP charter revision c59db20 (2026-09-24) chose nocx as the real repository for the skill's one-time check (madarch-utk); the server-views run then turned that one-time acceptance into a permanent test.

## Done when
- The server e2e test builds its second source itself: a fixture git repository it creates in a scratch folder, with a model that passes the check, sent with the real send command. No outside checkout and no variable naming another repository; the test runs on any clone under MADARCH_SERVER_E2E=1.
- Product messages, current specs, the glossary and tests use a neutral example name (github.com/acme/shop, which the spec already uses); `grep -ri nocx src test scripts docs/system docs/glossary.md` finds nothing.
- Disproved by: any test that needs a path outside the repository, or a product message naming nocx.

## Left out
- History stays as it is: closed change records (docs/changes/*), the MVP charter and decision records describe what happened then.
- The branch madarch-skill-run in the nocx repository: deleting it is the owner's call in their repository; ask, do not do it as part of this work.

title: Stage 2: madarch installs and runs on a clean Linux, macOS and Windows by npx, with no system OpenSSL
description:
Second stage of madarch-lfhu (charter outcome 5): the binary installs and runs on a clean machine of every platform the owner named, with `npx madarch` as the primary install.

Owner, 2026-10-13: asked what a person with nothing installed does first ("на первом пункте все и отвалятся"), then "А windows?"; agreed that the CLI does the setup and no Makefile is needed. No release exists yet (zero GitHub releases, nothing on npm), so today nobody can install madarch without cloning and building it.

Verified by the coordinator on 2026-10-13 (bun scripts/build-binary.ts --version 0.0.1, linux-x64, 89 MB): `madarch version` runs; `madarch new` dies with `libssl.so.3: cannot open shared object file` (ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED). `ldd` of @ladybugdb/core's lbugjs.node: libssl.so.3 and libcrypto.so.3 not found on this NixOS machine; the build's smoke (version, list) never touches the graph store, so it passed.

## Done when
- The binary needs no system OpenSSL: `madarch new` then `serve` work on a Linux with no libssl3 (e.g. Ubuntu 20.04 or Alpine/musl, or a NixOS shell without it), or the release names its exact system requirement and the installers check it with a clear message; the build's smoke runs `new` and opens the graph store, not only `version` and `list`.
- Windows x64: the release workflow builds `madarch-windows-x64.exe` on a Windows runner (LadybugDB ships @ladybugdb/core-win32-x64 0.20.4), the npm wrapper gains `@madarch/win32-x64`, and the script install has a PowerShell form. Windows arm64 is refused by name (no LadybugDB build).
- Clean-machine walks, one per platform (Linux x64, macOS arm64, Windows x64), each from nothing to a served product with the primary install `npx madarch new <name>` then `serve`, recorded in the acceptance record with the commands and their output.
- Left out: publishing (the release and the npm publish wait for the owner's yes); Windows arm64; `madarch repo add` (madarch-74k4).

title: madarch is the product's tracker: work items on the product's entities, exclusive reservations confirmed by a shared arbiter, offline work synced as operations, shown in madarch and driven by agents through CLI, API and MCP
description:

Charted by to-milestone when the owner schedules it; first steps per the source: end-to-end scenarios and conflict rules, a decision record, then a prototype of the arbiter (two clients, one reservation, transfer, resubmission), then offline children.

Running or choosing agents; a UI outside madarch; a second catalogue of product entities.

title: Link a product's work to an external tracker such as Jira: its items and status on the wiki's pages, then a two-way sync
description:
Owner, 2026-10-09 (decision 0017): many teams work in Jira and similar trackers. An external tracker is another adapter beside the product's own tracker. comments.author: shady2k
comments.text:
The set published setup in a product repository (skills-k8c part a) in shady2k-skills plugin 0.91.0, setup 0.41.0 (github.com/shady2k/skills main, 8a4c2e0).
- product.mjs adds `repo add <folder> <name> <url> [--branch <b>] [--json]` (enters a code repository in workspace.yaml's repos with one commit, every other byte kept; refuses a bad name, a duplicate, an unreadable manifest, a folder that is not its own git repository, uncommitted changes, a missing or option-like url; a failed commit restores the manifest) and `where [<folder>] [--json]` (product, code with the product root and repository name, or none; exit 2 on an unreadable manifest).
- Setup recognises a product repository (document places from the layout, its own tracker, the product-documents check as the commit gate) and a product's code repository (no tracker of its own; commit task ids resolve against the product's tracker at ../..; the backlog gate runs in the product repository; refused until the product repository is set up).
- The path from an empty folder: new, setup in the draft, rename, repo add, bootstrap, setup in the code repository. test/product-walk.test.mjs covers the programs end to end; setup itself is an agent-run skill with no code test.
This is what outcomes 2 and 5 of idea-to-wiki rely on for the commit check in a product repository and the first code repository. Moving write-intended-model (part b) is not scheduled.

title: Check a repository's product corpus with one versioned contract file
description:
Outcome 1 of knowledge-base (charter docs/milestones/knowledge-base.md, decision 0016). madarch's document contract (vision, requirements, decisions, glossary, the intended model with its scenarios and data entities, sources such as transcripts of conversations with product owners and the business, a path mapping for documents kept elsewhere) has its source in madarch and is built into one dependency-free file with --version, which a repository runs to check its corpus; the model check is part of it. The model skill lives in shady2k-skills and calls the installed file; madarch keeps no copy of it.

A requirement, a use case or a decision cites the source it came from by a quote and a place in it (a time or a line range); a source is kept in the repository or outside it, where the corpus keeps the quote and a reference.

## Left out
The skill set's own work (asking at setup where sources are kept and how they are redacted, its setup installing the file, onboarding, a documents-only mode) is tracked in its own repository.

## DONE WHEN
the built file, copied into a clean checkout of madarch, accepts madarch's corpus and prints its version; a broken corpus fixture is refused naming the file, the line and what is wrong; a fixture whose documents live at other paths passes through its mapping; a citation whose quote is not at the place it names in a source kept in the repository is refused naming both, and one to a source kept outside is reported as not verified; skills/write-intended-model is gone from madarch and madarch's model is checked by the contract file installed from the skill set.

comments.text: Owner decision 2026-10-08 (preflight of madarch-hnq, "Да, согласен"): three pieces. The contract file installed in each repository holds no graph: it loads, compiles and checks, and gives model.json. The madarch engine is installed once per machine (a package or a container) with LadybugDB (a 29 MB native library per platform): the local graph in a cache outside git, the wiki, a local MCP. The server is optional. A skill asks the local engine first, then a configured server, then reads model.json. title: Store the graph on a sound foundation
description:
The formats and storage everything else stands on: the intended-model YAML format (nesting to any depth; environments with bindings, zone differences and which elements each has; a chain of architecture states; no rules or flows yet), its compilation into model.json, the storage of every model version with valid and recorded time from the first write in SQLite, and LadybugDB as the query engine built from it, answering the views' traversals (collapse to the visible level, drill-in, transitive dependencies) with the time filter. Includes the walking skeleton: Bun (pinned 1.4.2), TypeScript, TypeBox, strict YAML, static and test commands. Decisions 0002, 0005, 0006, 0009, 0014, 0015. No HTTP server.

## DONE WHEN
conformance tests pass for the review's scenarios (a service gains internal elements and its relations keep their meaning; a service moves to another domain and its id and references stay; one request carries different data categories each way; two environments have different endpoints and zones; a general relation and its refinement are not counted twice); a model using environments and states compiles and is stored without loss; as-of reads on both time axes through the query engine return the expected graph.
close_reason: Outcome criterion holds on main: conformance scenarios pass end to end from YAML to query answers, a model with environments and states is stored and read back without loss, as-of reads on both axes through the query engine return the expected graph (bun test 322 pass, CI green at b82c517); change graph-foundation passed acceptance and close document checks

title: The server's vector index on pgvector and the local vector index on sqlite-vec: one adapter, never transferred
description:
Owner decision (2026-10-12 ~22:40 MSK, /tmp/madarch-run-iuc/note-storage-boundary.md, decision 0023): the vector index is sqlite-vec locally and pgvector on the server (in the same PostgreSQL that holds the fact log); full-text search sits in the same layer. Derived indexes are rebuilt from authored data and imported facts wherever they are needed and are NEVER transferred: the laptop and the server each build their own, possibly with different embedding models. The embedding model runs inside the image or at an internal company endpoint — no external API (the closed-network constraint, 0010).

## DONE WHEN (when opened)
The adapter serves embed/search behind one interface for both backends; a rebuilt index reproduces the search answers; an index of one mode is never shipped or transferred to the other; the embedding endpoint is configurable and the closed-network rule holds (no external API in default settings); review converged.

comments.text:
DONE

## 1. Recommendation

1. **No candidate fits: build the wiki thin inside madarch.** No engine meets requirements 1, 3 and 4 together — the git-native wikis (Gollum, OtterWiki, the Gitea/Forgejo wiki, SilverBullet) have no pre-write validation gate and no comments, and every rich wiki (Wiki.js, Outline, Docmost, BookStack, XWiki) makes a database authoritative instead of git.
2. **Keep madarch as the store and the write path**: the web UI calls madarch's own HTTP/MCP handler, which runs the document contract check first, refuses an invalid document, and only then writes the file and commits it with `git commit --author=<person>` in the product repository.
3. **Take the editing surface off the shelf, not the wiki**: CodeMirror 6 (MIT, plain-string document) for the first feature — the bytes that go in come out — with a madarch-rendered preview beside it; a WYSIWYG mode (MDXEditor, MIT, MDAST↔Lexical, string in and out) can come later as a per-user choice that rewrites a page deliberately (no WYSIWYG keeps Markdown byte-faithful).
4. **Comments as files beside the page** (one YAML file per thread per page, committed by the same path); git-bug is the closest prior art for sync semantics, but it stores in refs, so madarch defines this small format itself.
5. **Keep Starlight/Zensical as the read-only export and mermaid 12 for diagrams**, add Pagefind/Orama for search and better-auth/Auth.js for sign-in; the computed pages stay madarch's own work on the graph, not a wiki feature — so the next milestone's first feature should be the **write path**: edit a page, check it, and refuse it or commit it as its author, with the comments format and the local/central split following.

## 2. Candidate × requirements

Notation: **M** meets, **P** partly (with the reason), **B** breaks (with the reason). Requirements, abbreviated: **1** git is the store; **2** web edit = commit by its author; **3** validated before write, invalid refused; **4** comments in git next to the page; **5** computed pages + Mermaid; **6** agents write by the same path (madarch MCP); **7** same engine local and central, sync by plain git; **8** leaves madarch's LadybugDB graph alone; **9** TypeScript on Bun.

| Candidate | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 | 9 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Gollum** 6.1.0 (app 2024-12-23, lib 2025-10-20), MIT, Ruby | M git store, GitHub/GitLab-wiki compatible | P web UI yes, but the commit author is `session['gollum.author']`, which needs an external SSO front | B only post-facto hooks (`:post_commit`, `:post_wiki_initialize`); no pre-write hook, and its libgit2 commits do not run git hooks | B no comments (inline CriticMarkup only) | P renders Mermaid in a page; nothing computed | B HTTP JSON API, no MCP; rules are Ruby | M local and central, plain git | M no database | B Ruby (MRI/JRuby) |
| **Gitea/Forgejo wiki** (Gitea 28.1.0, 2026-10-06, MIT; Forgejo GPL-3.0), Go | M a real `.wiki` git repository per project | M commit author is the logged-in user (`doer.NewGitSig()`) | B hard-coded path/duplicate rules only; no document-form hook | B comments live on issues, not on wiki pages | B nothing computed | P REST API, no MCP | M plain git | M its index DBs are its own | B Go sidecar service |
| **OtterWiki** 2.25.0 (2026-10-03), MIT, Python | M content in a git repository | M web edit commits | B no hook or plugin system documented | B none | B Mermaid only | B no API for agents | M plain git | M no database | B Python/Flask |
| **SilverBullet** 2.12.0 (2026-10-06), MIT server (Desktop paid), Rust+TS | P files on disk are the source of truth, but nothing commits them | B saving writes a file; no git commit, no author | P `editor:pageSaving` event exists; whether it can veto is not established | B no threads | B its own query index, not git-derived | P HTTP API, no MCP | P its own sync engine, not git pull/push | P builds its own object index beside the graph | P TS client, Rust server |
| **Wiki.js** 3.0.0-beta.628 (2026-10-04, "not for production"), AGPL-3.0 | B the DB row is authoritative; the git module makes the **remote** authoritative on pull and replaces wiki content | P commits in the git mirror can carry the actor, but the DB is the live copy | B webhooks fire after the fact (`page:create/edit/...`); no pre-write gate | B external comment providers (disqus/giscus/...) or its own DB Talk view | P extension model, nothing computed from evidence | P 3.x GraphQL API, no MCP | P central service; a local instance keeps DB state you cannot discard and recreate | B its own `pageGraph`/`pageLinks`/`pageHistory` tables | P TS on Node, AGPL |
| **Outline** 1.10.1 (2026-09-09), BSL 1.1 (not open source; Apache-2.0 in 2030) | B Postgres is the store | P DB rows, author is a user id in the DB | P application-level validation only | P comments in the DB | P no evidence-derived pages | P REST/GraphQL, no MCP | P server with its own DB | B its own DB | P Node/TS, licence risk |
| **Docmost** 0.96.0 (2026-09-08), AGPL-3.0 | B Postgres + Redis store | P DB rows | P app validation | P DB comments | B | P no MCP | P | B own DB | P Node/TS |
| **BookStack** 26.09.1 (2026-09-29), MIT, PHP | B MySQL store | P DB rows | P app validation | P DB comments | B | B | P | B own DB | B PHP |
| **XWiki** 18.8.0 (2026-09-29), LGPL-2.1, Java | B Hibernate/RDBMS document store | P DB rows | P app validation | P DB comments | B | P REST | P | B own store | B Java platform |
| **Decap CMS** decap-cms@3.16.3 (2026-09-22), MIT | M host-API git only, no DB | M simple mode commits as the signed-in user; editorial workflow opens a PR per entry instead | P `required`/`pattern` validation in the browser (validators in `decap-cms-lib-widgets`); no server-side gate | B none | B none | B git-host API only; no MCP path | P works against any forge incl. self-hosted; the local proxy edits a folder and does not commit | M no database | P a host-page SPA (`import` takes over the page), not an importable component |
| **Sveltia CMS** v0.233.0 (2026-10-08), MIT | M git only | M remote commits in the editor's own account; B locally: the File System Access workflow writes files and leaves the commit to a git client | P field validation in the browser only | B none | B none | B no MCP | P | M no database | P SPA |
| **TinaCMS** tinacms@3.14.3 (2026-10-07), Apache-2.0 | P files in git are the source of truth, but a DB Data Layer is mandatory in front (self-hosting = your own Auth + Database + GitProvider) | M | P `ui.validate` in the editor; a server gate is yours to write | B none | B search/eval are TinaCloud's | B no MCP | P local `tina dev`; central via cloud or self-host | B its own cache DB | P React-first; a Bun app without React fights it |
| **Keystatic** @keystatic/core 0.6.9 (2026-08-26), MIT | M files or GitHub, no DB | B local mode writes files and makes no git calls; GitHub mode commits through your own GitHub App | P schema `validate` in the editor form | B none | B none | B no MCP | P | M no database | P React/Next-Astro-Remix route |
| **Starlight** 0.42.6 (2026-10-08), MIT — already used | M builds from the files | B static output, no write path | B nothing to validate against; export only | B none | P it renders madarch's computed pages and Mermaid; it computes nothing | B MCP is madarch's | M identical local and central, git is the only input | M no store of its own | M Astro/TS on Bun |
| **Zensical** 0.0.69 (2026-10-08), MIT — already used | M | B | B | B | P same as Starlight | B | M | M | M pinned Python tool run by `uvx` today |
| **Editors as parts** (CodeMirror 6, MDXEditor, Milkdown, TipTap, BlockNote) | n/a | P they are the editing surface, not the write path | P they can show errors but cannot refuse a commit | n/a | P they render nothing computed | n/a | n/a | n/a | P all TS; TipTap comments are paid, BlockNote Markdown round-trip is documented lossy |
| **Thin own app on madarch** (the recommendation) | M the working copy is the store; no database is added | M the handler writes the file and commits with `--author=<the signed-in person>` | M the contract check runs first and refuses; the file is written only when it passes | M one YAML file per thread beside the page, committed by the same path | M madarch already computes the pages and renders Mermaid; the new page kinds are madarch work | M one handler serves HTTP and the MCP server | M the same binary runs locally and centrally; sync is `git pull`/`git push` | M nothing new is authoritative over LadybugDB | M TypeScript on Bun, reusing `src/wiki` and the contract |

Notes on the table:
- Requirement 8 is "the wiki engine must not replace madarch's graph": a candidate **breaks** it when it keeps its own content database or graph tables (Wiki.js, Outline, Docmost, BookStack, XWiki, TinaCMS) and **meets** it when it holds no store of its own (Gollum, the Forgejo wiki, the CMSs' git mode, Starlight/Zensical).
- Requirement 9 is a cost, not a veto: Ruby/Python/Go/PHP/Java engines add a second runtime and a second write path that madarch cannot validate.
- "Comments" for the CMS row means page discussion; Bitbucket PR comments and Gitea labels are workflow status, not discussion.
## 3. The parts, if the app is thin

Everything below was read from the project's own docs/source or its registry metadata on 2026-10-09. The write-path invariant that makes the parts safe: **parse the candidate document to validate it, then write the original bytes to disk and commit them** — never re-serialize a page from an editor's internal model on the write path, because the serializers normalize (mdast-util-to-markdown's defaults rewrite bullets to `*`, quote marks and list indentation: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/syntax-tree/mdast-util-to-markdown/main/readme.md).

### Editor (the page surface)
- **CodeMirror 6 with `@codemirror/lang-markdown` 6.5.2** (MIT, 2026-08-04; the `codemirror` meta package is 6.0.2): a plain-string document, so what goes in comes out; the only transformations are ones a plugin applies. Source: https://registry.npmjs.org/@codemirror/lang-markdown
- **`@codemirror/lint` 6.9.7** (MIT, 2026-06-09) to show the contract check's findings at their line and column in the editor. Source: https://registry.npmjs.org/@codemirror/lint
- Optional later, per-user WYSIWYG: **MDXEditor 4.3.2** (MIT, 2026-10-02) — it converts MDAST ↔ Lexical, states "there is no intermediate HTML representation of the markdown document. The component accepts and emits markdown as a string", and ships a diff/source mode (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mdx-editor/editor/main/docs/overview.md, `.../docs/diff-source.md`). Alternative: **Milkdown 7.22.2** (MIT, 2026-09-23), whose source of truth is the ProseMirror document and whose output is remark-formatted (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Milkdown/website/main/docs/guide/faq.md). **TipTap 3.31.4** normalizes on serialize and its comments/review extensions are paid (https://registry.npmjs.org/@tiptap/markdown, https://tiptap.dev/pricing/). **BlockNote 0.55.0** documents its Markdown export as lossy and its `xl-*` packages as GPL-3.0/commercial (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TypeCellOS/BlockNote/main/docs/content/docs/features/export/markdown.mdx).
- Consequence for the recommendation: the byte-faithful surface is a source editor; WYSIWYG is a deliberate re-format of the page, which madarch can allow as a mode, not as the only way to write.

### Markdown parser and validator (the pre-write gate)
- **remark / unified**: `remark-parse` and `remark-stringify` 11.0.0 (MIT, 2023-09-18) over the documented **mdast** tree, with the plugin ecosystem for frontmatter, GFM and directives (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/remarkjs/remark/main/readme.md, https://registry.npmjs.org/remark-parse).
- **`remark-lint`** (MIT) — about 70 rules with presets, emitting `line:column` messages (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/remarkjs/remark-lint/main/readme.md); a project-specific rule is one remark plugin over the same AST.
- **`vfile-message` 4.0.3** (MIT) is the message type the check returns: `place` with `line`/`column`, plus `fatal`, `ruleId`, `source` (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vfile/vfile-message/main/readme.md) — exactly the "file, line and what is wrong" the contract check already promises.
- YAML side: **Ajv 8.20.0** (MIT) gives `instancePath` (a JSON Pointer) and `params` per error (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ajv-validator/ajv/main/docs/api.md); madarch already validates with typebox 1.3.34 (`package.json`), and a line number for YAML needs the parser's own position map (madarch has `src/model/yaml-position.ts`).
- Optional canonical form, if madarch wants byte-stable pages: **Prettier's `--check`** fails when a file is not formatted (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/prettier/prettier/main/docs/cli.md), with `proseWrap` defaulting to `preserve` so prose lines are not rewrapped (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/prettier/prettier/main/docs/options.md).

### Mermaid
- **mermaid 12.1.0** (MIT, 2026-10-02; madarch pins 12.0.0) draws in the browser. Server-side SVG needs a browser: **`@mermaid-js/mermaid-cli` 12.0.0** (MIT, 2026-09-24) launches Puppeteer (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mermaid-js/mermaid-cli/master/src/index.js). Measured here on Bun 1.4.2 with mermaid 12.0.0: `mermaid.parse` succeeds in-process, `mermaid.render` fails with "document is not defined"; madarch's own AGENTS.md already records headless Chromium with puppeteer-core working on this machine. Sources: https://api.github.com/repos/mermaid-js/mermaid/releases, https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid-cli

### Search
- **Pagefind 1.5.2** (MIT, 2026-04-12): it indexes the built static output and has no server component (https://pagefind.app/docs/) — the right part for the Starlight/Zensical export madarch already builds.
- **MiniSearch 7.2.0** (MIT, 2025-09-16): in-memory full-text, "can comfortably run both in Node and in the browser" (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lucaong/minisearch/master/README.md) — rebuild from git at boot; the least moving parts for a local wiki.
- **Orama `@orama/orama` 3.1.18** (Apache-2.0, 2025-12-19): in-process full-text/vector/hybrid for a long-lived server index (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oramasearch/orama/main/README.md).
- All three keep their index as derived data, so none becomes more authoritative than git.

### Auth (who the edit is attributed to)
- **better-auth 1.7.7** (MIT, 2026-09-30), framework-agnostic TypeScript auth (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/better-auth/better-auth/main/README.md); alternative **`@auth/core` 0.41.3** (ISC) used as a library, since `next-auth` v5 is still beta (5.0.0-beta.32, 2026-07-20).
- The honest limit, from git's own docs: author and committer names "have no effect on authentication" (https://git-scm.com/docs/git-commit), and GitHub's vigilant mode marks a commit "Partially verified" exactly when author ≠ committer (https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/managing-commit-signature-verification/about-commit-signature-verification). So madarch can attribute an edit (`git commit --author="Name <mail>"`, committer = the server, plus a trailer naming the person) and can sign with the **server's** key to prove the server wrote the commit; proving that the *person* authored it needs that person's key and is out of scope for a wiki whose trust model is the repository's own access control.

### Git access, concurrent edits, merge
- **The real `git` binary through `simple-git` 4.0.2** (MIT, 2026-09-26), with **one writer queue per repository** because git serialises index updates with lock files (`core.lockfilePid`, https://git-scm.com/docs/git-config). This is what keeps requirement 7 true: SSH remotes, credential helpers and hooks behave exactly as when a person runs git (https://git-scm.com/docs/gitcredentials, https://git-scm.com/docs/githooks); `--author`, `--date`, `--no-verify` and `-S` are documented options of `git commit`.
- **isomorphic-git 1.43.2** (MIT, 2026-10-08) is the fallback when no CLI is present (browser-only workspace, tests): `git.commit` takes author and committer objects and can sign via an `onSign` callback, but it speaks HTTP(S) only (SSH URLs are rewritten), runs no `.git/hooks`, ignores submodules and has no partial clone or wire protocol v2 (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/isomorphic-git/isomorphic-git/main/src/utils/translateSSHtoHTTP.js, `.../docs/onPrePush.md`, `.../src/commands/checkout.js`, `.../docs/faq.md`).
- Concurrent edits: **`git merge-file --object-id -p`** merges three blobs with no worktree or index, and **`git merge-tree --write-tree`** merges commits without touching the working tree (https://git-scm.com/docs/git-merge-file, https://git-scm.com/docs/git-merge-tree). A pure-JS equivalent is **node-diff3 3.2.1** (MIT, 2026-06-03); the older `diff3` package is dead (0.0.4, 2022-07-25, https://registry.npmjs.org/diff3). **Yjs** (13.6.33) and **Automerge** (3.5.0), both MIT, are only worth using as the editor's live layer: neither ships a Markdown/git adapter and their merge authority is the CRDT document, not the files (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yjs/yjs/master/README.md, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/automerge/automerge/main/README.md).

### Comments (there is no part to take)
- No candidate stores per-page discussion in git. The closest prior art for the *sync* half is **git-bug** (GPL-3.0, v0.11.0 2026-09-22), which keeps issues and comments in git refs so they travel with `git push`/`pull` (https://github.com/git-bug/git-bug); **git-appraise** stores reviews as git-notes and is unmaintained since 2023 (https://github.com/google/git-appraise, https://git-scm.com/docs/git-notes). So the comments format — one YAML file per thread beside the page, committed by the same path — is madarch's own small contract.

### The agent path (same write path)
- **`@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.32.1** (MIT, 2026-10-05, https://registry.npmjs.org/@modelcontextprotocol/sdk): the MCP server and the web UI call the same handler, so requirement 6 costs a transport, not a second write path.

### What stays unchanged
- **Zensical 0.0.69** and **Starlight 0.42.6** remain the read-only export: today's `src/wiki` already produces engine-neutral pages and hands them to either engine; a thin app adds a live surface beside them and does not replace them.
## 5. Citations
